summary: It Isn't Perfect, But I Still Love It!
reviewText:
I originally purchased a Surface Pro 4 top end before I bought this. You can not draw a line at an angle slowly without wobble/jitter, so I returned it. You can find videos on Youtube if you want to see it. Also, to be fair it felt like a plastic toy compared to the Cintiq.

The Good
 Built well! I love the rubber around the edges to hold onto it. The whole thing is well made for sure.
 No light bleed on my screen
 No dead pixels (My cintiq 13hd did and wacom wouldn't return it)
 Fast start up
 Feels like a cintiq meaning a very responsive pen
 Great colors (after screen protector is removed)
 You can outrun the pen if you really want to, but does a great job keeping up.

The Not So Good
 Fan noise. Honestly it isn't any louder than my Macbook Pro so I don't care. Don't expect ninja stealth mode with this guy. :)
 I thought the pen was lagging every time I would start a line, it wasn't. The tablet has "a hold for right click" so it would think it was pausing for a right click. Disabled that and it draws instantly.
 I disliked the graininess of the screen protector. I peeled that off after 5 minutes of use. Smoothness and glass are under it. This also makes the screen quality pop and look just as good as my Macbook. Note, this probably voids the warranty. :)

There are complaints about the battery life. This is a 13in screen running a full version of photoshop at 500 dpi, I don't expect to get 8 hours with it running. I was worried about the the 8gb of ram, but I haven't had it be a problem yet. Although with a huge brush at a huge dpi you can expect to outrun the pen. That is the same on almost any machine. You can ram, but Wacom did not make it easy to do.

I was reluctant to buy this Cintiq because all the bad reviews, but I'm so glad I did! I got the i7, 256, 8gb ram model. I love being able to go where ever I want to draw instead of lugging my computer and all the cables. I draw a lot more now that I have this as an option. Also, if I really want to do something overly complex I can still connect it just like the Cintiq 13HD to any computer!
matched_sentences: Note, this probably voids the warranty.

reviewText:
I am not an "audiophile" but I love my music and these headphones have been delightful to listen with.  I have had these for a couple of weeks and I have enjoyed the sound they give and the feel of the ear cushions. I use them with my phone, tablet and computer.  They are very comfortable on my head.  Slightly snug but I like that.  I don't like to wear headphones that feel like they are going to fall off all the time, but then I normally buy cheap headphones.

All the buttons on the cord work perfectly with my phone (Motorola Turbo 2) and I was told the microphone sounded great when I used it for a phone conversation.  The only disappointment is that the buttons do not work with my Asus Zenpad S 8 tablet.  I can pause the music which helps but the volume buttons do not work with it.  It's not a problem, just a tiny inconvenience (very tiny).  The description did say it works with "most" android devices so it wasn't guaranteed to work anyway.

I'm super happy with them otherwise. It made me a little nervous to spend this much on headphones without testing them first but for Christmas I was putting my trust in the brand that my son recommended.  I'm glad I did.

summary: Still the best protection for devices!
reviewText: So before I get into my review I want to let you guys know that I would of given this otterbox a 4.5 out of 5 because of two things that I will talk about later in my review. This is NOT my first otterbox I have had. I have had one for the iPhone 3GS, iPhone 5, iPhone 6+, iPad mini 1, iPad mini 2, Galaxy Tab A 9.7, and now this one for the iPad mini 4. As you can tell I have had many otterbox over the years because they provide me the protection that I need without looking or feeling bulky. No they are not perfect but they are the best protection out there and thats what I want for my expensive devices. In this review I want to talk about the feel of the otterbox, what its been like using it, who should buy it, pros and cons, and is it worth your money? (1.) Materials used, overall feel --- 4/5 So when I bought this from BestBuy about a month ago I was excited because I knew that I was getting the best protection for my new expensive device. As soon as I bought it I did not even make it to the car before I tore open the package and installed the otterbox on my new iPad mini 4 on the table at BestBuy. As soon as I opened it the hard plastic shell felt a little different, it felt somewhat flimsy. I was confused because the last otterbox I installed on my Galaxy Tab A felt hard as a rock. With no time to spare I quickly installed the case on my clean iPad before any dust could make it under the built in screen protector. Now that it was completely installed it felt great to hold. The rubber covering everything felt nice and firm, it did not feel cheap in the least bit. I also noticed immediately that the sides now feel different since it has this certain pattern to it. To me it feels better to hold for longer periods of time. I have also noticed that there is NO AIR GAP between the screen protector and the device itself. This is a huge plus to me since my old otterbox for the iPhone 6+ had a air gap which made it much harder to use my touch screen. I thought to myself, if it makes my device harder to use why do I want it? It got so bad and annoying as hell I ended up giving the otterbox to my friend who now uses it and instead bought myself a tempered glass screen protector and slim case for my 6+ which I still use till this day but anyways, the screen protector that is built into this otterbox for the iPad mini 4 is great! I am happy that I don't have to apply a ton of pressure to my screen to use it. One last thing I have noticed and not to happy with is that the rubber right above the charging port gets loose so so easy. I cant explain how easy it is to get it loose. No this may not seem like a big deal but over time it will get looser and looser which is unfortunate. Maybe I am wrong (and hope so to) but it really seems like that it will get worse over time. Overall the materials for this otterbox are great! I don't think this otterbox is as durable as the older otterboxes but its still more then enough for most people like myself. (2.) What its like using the otterbox --- 5/5 So far this otterbox is great. I have been able to put my iPad mini in my backpack with other things without having to worry about my iPad breaking or scratching. The otterbox comes with a hard plastic face shield that snaps on the four corners of the case to protect the screen from falls, scratches and just about everything except liquid. The face shield also acts as a stand to lay your device back on it to prop it up at a comfortable angle. I have noticed that this otterbox does add weight (no surprise) but with the protection it offers I really don't mind. For me it does not add so much weight that it make it unusable, its just enough weight to notice. If weight is going to bother you I strongly recommend buying tempered glass screen protector and a hard plastic snap on case. This case (just like any otterbox) has all the cut outs for all the ports and it does not get in the way of the volume switch or power button. I have FULL ACCESS to my device. It also has a light film over the home button to allow you to use touch ID. I am happy to see the otterbox company do this instead of leaving a hole there to allow dust to get in under the screen like the iPhone 5s otterbox. Overall this case does feel premium and does feel like if I were to drop my iPad that it won't break. This otterbox also has the light plastic film over the home button to allow you to use touch ID without letting dust under the screen. (3.) Who should buy this otterbox? 4/5 I think this fully protective case is for the people who want maximum protection without making your device look bulky and ugly. This otterbox feels as good as it looks and that is saying a lot. Most case either look ugly but offer decent protection or look fantastic but offer little to no protection. Otterboxes in general look great while offering the best protection. The only case that I can think of that offers more overall protection would be the life proof case since it is a waterproof case that offers close to the same protection as the otterbox. I bought this otterbox because I knew that it will keep my iPad looking as good as it did on day one. If you are somebody who wants a waterproof case I would recommend buying the life proof case because it still looks great but it also offers full water protection and protection from falls and scratches. If you are somebody who absolutely hates adding any type of weight but still wants to protect your device I would recommend buying a hard clear snap on case and tempered glass screen protector. This way you will be able to at least have some protection from scratches and small drops. Nothing is worst than having a shattered screen that you cant even use because you are afraid of cutting yourself. (4.) Pros and Cons Pros 1. Offers full rugged protection 2. Materials used feel very good to hold 3. Has all cut outs for ports and speakers 4. Built in screen protector that protects from scratches 5. Allows you to use touch ID with no problem 6. Looks very nice much better than most rugged case (cough cough griffin case) 7. Comes in 3 colors. Pink, Navy blue, Black 8. One year warranty 9. No air gap between screen protector and the device!!! Woohoo! Cons ): 1. Price! I paid $70.00 for mine at BestBuy 2. Cant use other iPad mini otterboxes for the iPad mini 4 3. No water protection 4. Adds some weight which may turn some people away 5. Can be very hard to install without getting dust under screen protector 6. The outer rubber will wear down over time 7. Hard to take off, ones its on its meant to stay on (5.) Is it worth the money? 5/5 For most people like myself I would have to say yes! Yes I understand it is not a perfect case but what is? It makes your device heavier and cost a chunk of change but what you get is full body protection and a good built in screen protection. I cant stress this enough, even though it is a rugged case it still looks better than most cases while offering the best protection. I have seen YouTube videos of people dropping their device in the otterbox from 100 feet, from space and from 3 stories high and the device still survives! If you really don't know if you should spend the $70.00 then ask yourself this. Do I want to keep my device looking as new as it did 2 or 3 years ago? If you are not worried about keeping your device in pristine condition then this case isn't for you. Also if you are not sure about buying it Id say go to the store and look at it for yourself. Im pretty sure the people at the store will let you try it on before buying it. Overall I defiantly think this case is worth the money Conclusion In the end I am very happy with my purchase. I feel like it is money well spent, keeping my $600.00 device protected from everyday use while still looking good. I am also happy with how it feels since most cheap cases feel like plastic and break within a month, this otterbox will last me at least a year if I treat it right. Everybody who reads my full review please know that I enjoy doing this, helping people out making good decisions on what to buy and what not to buy. I do my best to be as descriptive as I can. Please let me know how I did in the comments below, let me know what I can improve on or if I did a good job. (: Thanks for reading my review!

reviewText:
My computer is from 2011 (mobo accepts only up to a 3rd gen intel Core cpu) and the monitor is 1080p max.  I wasn't even going to bother upgrading the video card...until I saw how low the prices were on these 970s.

Many sellers are dumping 970s cheap because of the 3.5 VRAM issue.  If you take your time, you can get a like-new condition used FTW+ (top of the line 970) for under $200.  The 970 isn't the best card in the world, but (for nvidia) the specification to price ratio is great.

Buying used computer parts isn't always the best idea, but I just made sure the one I bought was a first owner card, wasn't user-overclocked and not too old...and got one in mint condition that still has 2.5 years left on the warranty.

The other thing I love about this card is the built-in DVR chip.  All nvidia GTX 600 and higher have this extra chip that, in conjunction with their free Shadowplay software, allows users to record anything (video, etc) they can see on their monitor....and it uses next to zero of your systems resources.

summary: Quiet compared to stock coolers, Performs slightly worse, and has fragile mounting hardware. But it looks Okay.
reviewText:
This cooler does not perform better than the stock cooler. that needs to be put out there right away. If you are looking for better cooling to maybe achieve a better overclock, this is not the cooler for you. this cooler is however orders of magnitude more quiet than the stock coolers from both intel and amd. so aesthetics and noise reductions are the only 2 reasons you should consider this cooler. in my case, that's what i needed.

Now let's get down to the good the bad and the ugly.

the good, is the packaging and the aesthetics. The packaging is up there with what you would expect from popular brands. it has a full spec sheet on the side including the supported sockets and fan size/speed(rpm). It also looks clean overall. Along with the cooler itself, the package includes a ton of mounting hardware, so you know they aren't kidding when they put that huge list of supported sockets on the box. It also includes thermal paste that is not pre applied. for me this was good, since it saved me the time of cleaning it off to apply the stuff I prefered. but for some, having to apply the included paste out of a little paper bag is not going to be a good or clean experience.

the bad, is the performance. it is absolutely 100% guaranteed to perform worse than any intel or amd stock cooler. and that's just how it is. this design is a very generic one used by a lot of no-name over-seas sellers, and no matter who you buy it from it always seems the majority of reviews would agree that it's just overall not great at cooling.

the ugly, is the mounting hardware. while it supports a ton of sockets, the mounting hardware was cheaply made. the AM3 mount specifically requires you to change the level of the included clips, and to do that you have to bend extremely fragile metal bits on the edges. basically you can expect this to break the mounting clips 9 out of 10 times. luckily they stil hold the cooler in place once properly aligned, but this makes it extremely difficult to actually hold in place to mount. overall the mounting hardware really compromised quality for quantity of supported sockets.

Overall , you really have to be wanting better aesthetics and less noise for this cooler to be worth it. but for the price, if that is what you want, then this cooler might fit the bill.
matched_sentences: it is absolutely 100% guaranteed to perform worse than any intel or amd stock cooler.

summary: UPDATED: Good camera and sensor with quirks and some early quality issues, but reliable since
reviewText:
This is a long-term perspective I am sharing for anyone considering this camera, as it is still being sold. First, I am a Nikon devotee, and own other Nikon cameras going back to film SLRs; so assessing 3 stars isn't easy for me.  Although the D5300 has proven itself to take wonderful pictures, it has unfortunately been plagued with some odd quirky issues and serious quality problems.  Both my wife and I will still use it on occasion when we want that additional crop sensor reach.

UPDATE November 2017:  I preface this update by acknowledging this is a "long after the buying decision" retrospective.  This particular model will soon no longer offered as new.  I am updating the 3 stars to 4 stars based on the following:  The issue reported concerning the mode switch was due to the foil decal on top of the knob having shifted.  There is a key to align it, but somehow it became dislodged.  The AF malfunction was unfortunate, but has been corrected by factory service, as originally noted.  Overall, the camera has been reliable since.

The good stuff:
- Great sensor - low noise, really seems to do well with mid tones
- Focus tracking is pretty solid
- LCD (swivels) is sharp and readable in all conditions

The not-so-good stuff:
- My camera lost AF entirely after a few months of use (tried several different lenses) and had to be shipped back to Nikon service for repair.  It was fixed, however I was without this camera for almost 2 weeks.
- (FIXED) The rotary mode switch is flaky, and now doesn't match up with the actual mode in use.  For instance, the knob reads shutter priority while it is actually set to aperture priority mode (issue arose after warranty period).
- Some SD card brands have proven to show intermittent card read errors (Transcend, Lexar) - this was even after formatting.  SanDisk Ultra have worked OK.
- Though I do like the 18-140 kit lens, the camera feels very front-heavy and awkward to hold due to the small grip.
- Needing to use front button to toggle ISO is not intuitive and takes a concerted effort.
- Menu isn't too easy to navigate.

Overall, beyond some of the inconveniences, this camera is competent and takes lovely pictures.  The quality issues I have experienced may simply be a run of bad luck, however, it has somewhat tainted my perception of Nikon quality.
matched_sentences: For instance, the knob reads shutter priority while it is actually set to aperture priority mode (issue arose after warranty period).

summary: No semaphore timeout error on Dell's XPS 8700 PC; Works well initially then randomly drops communication
reviewText:
I can pass along that on Dell's 8700 XPS tower PC from 2014, this enclosure does not have the semaphore timeout issue some external enclosures/burners have.  This is no guarantee you won't experience it on your PC.  It's an issue involving a conflict between the SATA to USB bridge controller in the enclosure and your SATA/USB controller on the motherboard in your PC.  The only way, generally, to resolve it is to replace your motherboard or the enclosure.  Since it's cheaper and easier to replace the entire PC versus just the motherboard, it's not as easy or cheap, though, as just replacing the enclosure.  Unfortunately, the only way you'll know for sure if your PC doesn't have this issue is to try this enclosure.

EDIT: 2018-06-10 - Changed my review.  It seemed to work fine, but after more thorough testing with different drives, media, and on different PC's, it has one fatal flaw that I cannot recommend this unit for.  It randomly drops communication with the device.  The drive lights will still be flashing indicating it's doing something, but the actual write/verify rate in ImgBurn will be 0.0x.  Cancelling the operation in ImgBurn leaves ImgBurn in an infinite loop until you power off the enclosure.  This can, and has, caused me to waste a writable disc because communication was dropped with the device.

This has happened on a Dell XPS 8700 and 8930, with an LG and a Pioneer burner, on DVD+RW and BD-R.  So, the problem is the enclosure.

This unit seemed to work well for a while and then started doing this.  I don't know if this means the device always did this and I just happened to get lucky in that it didn't do it before.  Or if this unit is faulty or simply this device is not very good quality.  Either way, I can't recommend this product anymore after my experiences.

I'm going to try the OWC Mercury Pro next.
matched_sentences: This is no guarantee you won't experience it on your PC.

reviewText:
I'll give you a play-by-play review of my experience with this product as a new user. I'll put a + by the things I like, and a - by the things I don't like. (multiples represent more than one element being scored, and/or, intensity of my reaction)
+1) I like the packaging. It's stylish, modern, and EASY to open. No sealed clamshell edges. Attractive colors and clean design.
+2) Easy to remove from packaging.
+3) I found that it has 3 sets of foam earpieces in small, medium and large. So Baby, Mamma and Papa Bear will all be accommodated for individual comfort. Well done.
+4) Little instruction book (in several languages) is easy to locate and the instructions are clear.
-5) I went to turn on the unit and found that it has no battery charge. I hate that.
+6) It does have a 3" USB/Micro USB cord for charging.
--7) Upon reading through the instructions, I discovered that a) there is no reference to battery life anywhere, so I have no idea how long I can use the product without recharging, and b) the design does not admit replacement of the battery.

POSSIBLE DEAL-KILLER: In the words of the instruction book: "Note: Your battery is designed to last THE LIFE OF THE PRODUCT [my emphasis added]. It should only be removed by a recycling facility. Any attempt to remove or replace your battery may damage the product and void your warranty." Several issues with this. First, the life of the product is basically defined as the life of the battery. Not impressed with that. Second, the language is a little vague on whether or not you actually have a warranty if you attempt to replace the battery, which, for all intents and purposes, means *you have no warranty if you replace the battery.* Furthermore, there is no indication of how long one might expect the battery to last. For a product of this cost, this seems like a fatal flaw in planning and design.

----8) Still waiting for the battery to charge. The product does not function or show up on blue tooth while it's in charging mode. And there's no indication in the instructions on how long the initial charge should take. It only says to charge it until the indicator light turns green. I really dislike the uncertainty, and it seems it would be easy to give me some answer to an obvious question that any user will have. If I were designing the packaging or instruction manual, I'd put a big notice: "Plug in your unit to a power source right away! Within [x amount of time] you will be able to continue your setup, begin using your head set, and then manage the rechargeable battery to enjoy [thousands?] of hours of listening on your VerveRider!" As it is, I'm just feeling annoyed that I have to charge it and I have no idea how long I'm waiting. Bad first impression. Again, they could manage this for a much better user experience. Disappointing.

-9) There is no wall charge piece. Bummer that. How hard would that be? There's definitely room in the package for such an inexpensive add-on. Another strike.

+10) Okay, approximately 30 minutes in, the indicator light has turned green to indicate it is charged.

+11) Once the device is charged, simply turn on the power button and activate it on the Blue Tooth of [my iPhone] and it gives an audible announcement through the earplugs: "Pairing complete. Device connected."

+12) You actually have the option to pair it with more than one device - so if you have an iPad and an iPhone (or whatever), you can link both to your VerveRider (weird name. I think I would have enjoyed that meeting.).

13) When I first attempted to use the earbuds the volume was REALLY low. Just to be clear, the unit doesn't control the hand device volume (which I had set very low). For me to hear it well I had to turn up my hand device volume all the way, and then adjust the headset control. No problem at all with volume.

14) Sound quality is actually pretty good. Doesn't blow me away as the best ever, but honestly - no serious complaints. Bass is a little bit weak on my TV viewing, but I can still hear all low the tones really clearly (as well as the beatboxing) on my favorite a capella group in the Music app, and I think that's a pretty good test.

So performance is actually good; but since I don't feel confident of the useful life of the device (and that confidence is pretty much the point of reading reviews, IMHO), I have to give it a middlin' rating.

reviewText:
We purchased this 1X1 80-mile antenna/preamp combo during the Prime Day sale event, to replace a 40-year-old rooftop antenna. Most of July the days were 100%F or more, so we waited to install the antenna for 2 weeks, until it was cool enough to work on the roof. The antenna is mounted 20 feet above the front porch and attached 4 feet above the roof peak on the pole. Wife actually enjoyed assembling the antenna by a couple of glanced at the instruction page. The antenna is very lightweight, appearing so small and delicate it makes our old 10+foot channel master antenna look as large as the ISS in comparison.
A couple of months prior to purchasing the 1X1 unit, a severe storm sent a tree into the rear portion of the roof, and bent the channel master antenna in half. The 1X1 antenna was the first rooftop I'd put up since the transition from analogue to digital, and I was hoping it would be sufficient. All of the feedback and reviews I've researched here and elsewhere, indicated this was a good choice for our location. With all respect to 'leaf' advanced design types of newer antennas, I'm still unconvinced that paying 4-times the price of this unit, wouldn't actually benefit us.
We're near the crest of what most city folks would consider a small mountain; the national antenna coverage map indicates it's a fringe area, but we're only 20 miles from the nearest CBS affiliate as the crows fly and approximately 60 miles to the PBS tower.  After connecting the preamp into the coax at our 4K TV and powering it up, on the first channel scan we were rewarded with all of the channels we expected to see, 15 OTA networks. Since the date of installation, there have been several mornings when due to signal skip/bounce, we've briefly seen a few low-powered stations located as far as 160 miles distant, but that's unusual for our location. Several mornings I've picked up St. Louis affiliates from the reverse angle, at 100 miles away; that's not shabby for the specs of this unit and the sale price we paid.
If the July heat wave hadn't broken, we would've installed this unit upstairs in the dormer, but Wife nixed that idea, something about drilling holes didn't appeal to her. Some folks have remarked they've had success with that method, and submitted some very nice photos. We finally got everything functioning well about 2 weeks after the order arrived. Then, 2-weeks post installation, I powered our systems up only to discover we had a paltry 4 stations showing up on the first scan and found the small white LED/power pilot light on the preamp wasn't lit, indicating a dead preamp. I sent a query to 1X1, to see if they'd be willing to honor the 12-month warranty, and since it was during the weekend, while I waited patiently for their reply, I removing the failed preamp and reinserted the channel master preamp in place of the 1X1 preamp. I was instantly rewarded when 9 channels appeared on the first scan. Subsequent scans showed as 6 or as many as 11 stations, but we never went above 11 until the replacement unit arrived.
We received a reply from 1X1 on Monday; I documented the installation and subsequent failure of the antenna preamp, and 1X1 reached the same conclusion, that the preamp was DEAD. They arranged to ship a warranty replacement (please see the 1X1 vender review). 1X1 went a step further, since we don't have 'normal' mail service, and can't receive mail or packages, 1X1 had the shipment intercepted and delivered via regular UPS service. This wasn't light speed by any means, but we were pleased with their response and warranty service.
As soon as the replacement preamp arrived, the channel master preamp was removed, the new 1X1 was inserted, and the first scan provided the same 15 channels we expected to have. To be sure, the new preamp has a red LED, so if it ever fails again (perish the thought) I see it immediately.
One morning the channel scan registered 23 channels, but those just don't last; the first preamp never went above the 15 we expect, and it just doesn't get better than it's designed for. As a side note, all of our electronics, from PCs to the 4K TV and audio/visual gear is plugged in and powered by several UPS power/battery backup units; this isn't so we can watch TV or be on the internet if the power goes out, but to protect from voltage under/overages. When the weather looks like it's going to kick up, we unplug everything, especially the antenna coax where it comes down from the roof; it's grounded, but lightning rarely cares about an antenna ground if it hits your house. In all the years we've done it this way, we've never lost any gear due to power or weather issues. The TV and antenna preamp are on their own power cut-off switch, so I can shut it down quickly, rather than having to pull the plug on the UPS each time. I run a small, noiseless ventilation fan to cool not only the electronics and CPU in the 4K TV cool, but the attached modules and amplifiers; keeps it all living longer, if not prospering.
I hope the review helps our fellow Amazonians make good purchasing decisions for themselves and their families; as always, my opinions are my own and are submitted without any compensation. I'm confident if we ever needed to contact 1x1 again for assistance or warranty replacement, they will continue to offer the same friendly support we received this time.

summary: Excellent Upgrade for TiVo Roamio OTA
reviewText: I bought the Western Digital 2 TB WD AV-GP SATA III Intellipower 64 MB Cache Bulk/OEM AV Hard Drive WD20EURX hard drive to increase the storage capacity of a TiVo Roamio OTA. Ive read in other reviews, some buyers are receiving used or refurbished hard drives. I did not want to install a used or refurbished hard drive. I contacted the seller, TNTelectron, and I was assured the drive shipped would be new. The hard drive I received was manufactured in May 2014, over two years ago, and I was concerned a used drive had been shipped. Using CrystalDiskInfo, I accessed the hard drives SMART data. The disc health is good and here are two pertinent readings: Power on Count: 5 Power on Hours: 0 The SMART data show the drive has only been powered on 5 times previously and hasn't even reached one hour of use. I am pleased but I wonder where this drive has been for the past two years and if its not actually refurbished with the drive data erased during the process. In any event, the price was good, the warranty from the seller is 1-year replacement, and, as of this writing, 30 days since installing the hard drive, everything is working well. After installing the hard drive and powering on the TiVo Roamio, the replacement hard drive made quite a bit of noise. I was concerned I did something wrong but after a minute or so the drive quieted down. Now, if I get close to the TiVo I can hear the spindle spinning but its very faint and not an issue for me. The drive has been working quietly for almost 30 days and no issues. Im pleased with the hard drive and the seller, TNTelectron. Below are some comments regarding installing the Western Digital WD AV-GP 2TB hard drive into the TiVo Roamio OTA. TiVo has apparently made some changes over time. I have read elsewhere different size tools have been used. I used the following tools with the TiVo Roamio OTA manufactured in April 2015: T8 Torx screwdriver for the back of the unit screw. T10 Torx screwdriver for the hard drive and the hard drive rails Flat head screwdriver to gently pry the cover away from the base to gain access Installing the drive was actually very easy. Disconnect the TiVo from all the cables and power. Remove the screw on the back in the center of the unit with a T8 torx screwdriver Gently use a flat head screwdriver to pry the cover away from the base. To remove the cover, I gently pulled up the cover enough to create a small gap between the cover and the base at the back of the unit. I inserted the flathead screwdriver at the edge and gently rotated it left and right and proceeded to go around the edges. As I did, the cover released from the base. Once the cover is off, the hard drive is visible. Use a T10 torx screwdriver to remove the three screws holding the drive to the unit. Disconnect the power and data cable from the hard drive and remove the hard drive. Next, remove the rails from the hard drive using the T10 screwdriver. Now, attach the rails to the replacement hard drive. Attach the power and data cable to the replacement hard drive. Place the replacement hard drive into the unit and tighten the screws previously removed. Place the cover back over the unit. I first made sure the clip in the front of the unit matched up and then the rest of the cover easily clicked into place. Reconnect the TiVo to start the new setup process. TiVo Roamio automatically formatted the drive. All One Passes (i.e. Season Passes) and preferences will need to be set again. According to the System Information, I now have 316 hours of HD recording capacity.
matched_sentences: In any event, the price was good, the warranty from the seller is 1-year replacement, and, as of this writing, 30 days since installing the hard drive, everything is working well.

reviewText:
I purchased this TV from Amazon in January, 2014. In the last month, THE problem (faulty capacitor) noted in the other negative reviews here has surfaced. The TV will simply not turn on when the power switch is depressed. Pulling the AC plug and re-plugging allows the TV to power on ... some of the time. But eventually, it doesn't and the plug/re-plug scenario has to be repeated. I called Samsung tech support, got a polite rep with a foreign accent on a horrendous VoIP line that was filled with static and noise. After taking down my information, he gave me the phone number of a local "service center" that's closed at the moment. I checked their web site -- they "provide healthcare facilities with excellent service and quality repairs."  There's nothing on their web site about repairing consumer electronics! I'll try them in the morning; I'm sure this will be good for a laugh. Will report back tomorrow. I suspect this TV will be headed to the recycling center and I'll be buying a new one. But no more Samsung products for me ... EVER! (BTW, I discovered after purchasing this piece of junk that it doesn't even have a headphone jack for private listening.)

NEXT DAY UPDATE: I called the "service center" that the Samsung rep recommended. As I suspected, they have NOTHING TO DO WITH REPAIRING CONSUMER ELECTRONICS! I called Samsung again this morning and informed them of the problem. They gave me the name of another service company ... 100 miles from where I live!  The Samsung rep informed me that my TV was not covered by the warranty and that they would not pay to have the TV repaired. The new service center's website quoted rates of $200 or more. (And I doubt they would travel 200 miles round trip to fix a TV.) So adios to Samsung.

NEW UPDATE: I contacted the Samsung CEO's office via email (you can Google it), explained the problem, and received a very nice response fairly quickly.  They asked me to submit proof of purchase and a few days later received an email informing me that Samsung would pay the parts and labor to have my TV repaired. So Samsung has gone WAY UP in my book.
